tools.title: Security Tools
tools.subtitle: Ciphers, encoding, hashing, and password generator

caesar.title: Caesar Cipher
caesar.description: Shifts each letter of the alphabet by a fixed number of positions.
caesar.example: Example: "HELLO" with shift 3 → KHOOR. Used by Roman general Caesar for secret correspondence. Vulnerable to frequency analysis — easily cracked with text longer than 20 characters.

vigenere.title: Vigenere Cipher
vigenere.description: Uses a keyword for variable shifting of each letter. Long considered unbreakable.

xor.title: XOR Encryption
xor.description: Bitwise exclusive OR. Encryption and decryption are the same operation.
xor.property: Property: A XOR B XOR B = A. So the same XOR operation both encrypts and decrypts. XOR is used in OTP (One-Time Pad) — the only theoretically unbreakable cipher, if the key is truly random and used only once.

base64.title: Base64
base64.description: Encodes binary data as text. Used for data transmission in JSON, email (MIME), Data URLs in HTML/CSS. Base64 is NOT encryption! Anyone can decode the data.

urlEncoding.title: URL Encoding / Decoding
urlEncoding.description: Encodes special characters in URLs. Essential skill for XSS and CSRF work — understanding how browsers interpret encoded characters.
urlEncoding.securityNote: Security connection: URL encoding can bypass WAFs. For example, <script> can be encoded as %3Cscript%3E. Some filters check the decoded version, others don't.

hashing.title: Hash Functions — Visualization
hashing.description: A hash function converts input data of arbitrary length into a fixed-length string. Changing even one input character completely changes the hash. A hash is one-way: the original data cannot be recovered.
hashing.avalancheNote: Even a single character change completely alters the hashing result — this is called the "avalanche effect".

passwords.title: Password Generator
passwords.description: Generates cryptographically strong passwords using Web Crypto API.
passwords.managersDescription: Generating passwords isn't enough — you need to store them securely. Use trusted password managers that encrypt the vault with a master password:
passwords.keepassxc: Local storage, open source, browser plugins

aes.title: AES-like Encryption (Demo)
aes.description: Demonstration of symmetric encryption. Real AES-256-GCM uses Web Crypto API with a 256-bit key, IV, and authentication tag. This demo shows the working principle.
aes.note: Note: This is a simplified demonstration. Real AES-256-GCM uses SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, and AddRoundKey rounds. Use Web Crypto API.

jwt.title: JWT Decoder
jwt.description: JSON Web Token consists of 3 parts: Header (algorithm), Payload (data), and Signature. Data is encoded in Base64URL — paste a token to decode.

rot13.title: ROT13
rot13.description: A special case of the Caesar cipher with a shift of 13. Since the English alphabet has 26 letters, ROT13 restores the original text twice: ROT13(ROT13(x)) = x.
rot13.example: Example: "Hello World" → Uryyb Jbeyq. Used on forums to hide spoilers. Not encryption — doesn't protect data since there's no key.

tools.aesError: Error: invalid key or corrupted data
tools.jwtPartsError: JWT must contain 3 parts separated by dots

bruteforce.title: Brute Force Visualization
bruteforce.description: Find out how long it takes to crack a password based on length and complexity.
bruteforce.recommendation: Recommendation: Use passwords 12+ characters long with uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters. Such a password would take hundreds of years to crack even on powerful GPU clusters.

hashing.demoDescription: Enter a password to see how bcrypt hashing with salt works.
hashing.autoSalt: Automatically adds salt — protection from rainbow tables
hashing.adjustableCost: Adjustable cost factor — slows down brute force
hashing.oneWay: One-way — impossible to recover password from hash

otp.title: Interactive TOTP Demo (Time-based One-Time Password)
otp.description: TOTP generates a one-time 6-digit code that changes every 30 seconds. This is a second authentication factor — even if an attacker learns the password, they can't log in without this code.
otp.hint: Hint: copy the code above and paste it to verify
otp.step1Desc: Server generates a random secret (usually 16-32 Base32 characters) and shares it with the user (QR code).
otp.step2Desc: Client and server compute HMAC-SHA1 from the secret and current time step (timestamp / 30).
otp.step3Desc: 4 bytes are extracted from HMAC, converted to a 31-bit number, then modulo 10^6 = 6-digit code.
otp.step4Desc: Server compares client's code with its own computation. ±1 step (30 sec) is allowed to compensate for network delay.
without2faItems: Password only — single point of failure
with2faItems: Protection from phishing and brute force

sessions.title: Session Security
sessions.jwtDescription: JWT is a compact token for transmitting information between client and server. Consists of three parts: Header (algorithm), Payload (data: user ID, role, expiry) and Signature (integrity check). Tokens can be stored in localStorage or HttpOnly cookies.

sqlInjection.title: SQL Injection Lab
sqlInjection.subtitle: Interactive environment for learning SQL vulnerabilities
sqlInjection.hint1Text: Try to understand the structure of the SQL query and find the injection point.
sqlInjection.hint2Text: Pay attention to quote syntax, comments, and UNION operators.
sqlInjection.notSqlInjection: This doesn't look like SQL injection
sqlInjection.trySuggestions: For SQL injection try: single quotes, SQL keywords (OR, UNION SELECT, --), or other constructions. Click Example for a hint.
sqlInjection.protectionText: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) or ORM libraries (Prisma, Sequelize, TypeORM). Never insert user input directly into SQL queries via string concatenation.

csrf.csrfDescription: CSRF is an attack where an attacker forces a browser of an authenticated user to perform an unwanted action on a site where the user is already authorized. The attack exploits the fact that the browser automatically attaches authentication cookies to every request to the domain for which they are set.

owaspTop10.congratsAll: Congratulations! You have studied all 10 critical OWASP Top 10 threats.

owaspTop10.whyImportantText: This vulnerability is part of OWASP Top 10 — the list of the most critical threats for web applications. Understanding this category is essential for every developer.

owaspTop10.vulnerableCodeTitle: Vulnerable Code — What NOT to Do
owaspTop10.vulnerableWarningText: The code shown contains vulnerabilities. Do not use similar patterns in production. Each line with a "VULNERABLE CODE" comment demonstrates a typical developer mistake.
owaspTop10.secureCodeTitle: Secure Code — How to Do It Right
owaspTop10.secureNoteText: Secure code always includes input validation, access control checks, and error handling. The difference between vulnerable and secure code often comes down to a few lines of checks.
owaspTop10.mitigationsTipText: Apply these recommendations comprehensively. A single protection method is rarely sufficient — use "Defense in Depth".
